chunks: And through it, from Ibn Sinan, from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna al-Attar, from Abdullah ibn Bakr; and al-Hakam narrated from Abu Ja'far that he said:
How will you be if you go up and do not find anyone, and you return and do not find anyone!

key_terms.أَحَدًا: Anyone (referring to the Imam or a guide)
key_terms.صَعِدْتُمْ: You go up / ascend (metaphorically for seeking or approaching)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the condition of people when they cannot find him during the occultation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (as) poignantly captures the existential anxiety of the Shia community during the Major Occultation, where the physical absence of the Imam creates a sense of spiritual disorientation. It underscores the transition from direct, tangible guidance to a period of waiting (Intizar), emphasizing the psychological impact of searching for the Imam's presence only to find him veiled from view. This rhetorical question serves as a reminder of the community's reliance on internal spiritual connection when external leadership is hidden.
